🇲🇽🏘️ <u>MEXICO CITY BUILDS THE CARE ECONOMY: CASA DE LAS 3 RS</u>

Mexico City keeps turning care into public policy. The Casa de las 3 Rs del Cuidado — recognize, redistribute, reduce — brings free medical attention, training workshops and community services directly into the colonias, framed as a shared responsibility between society and government institutions. While elsewhere care work stays invisible and unpaid, CDMX is building the infrastructure to redistribute it.

🇲🇽🎓 <u>UNAM TO RE-TEST 58,000 APPLICANTS IN PERSON AFTER ADMISSIONS SCANDAL</u>

UNAM is cleaning house after the online admissions fiasco. Around 58,000 selected applicants will retake a supervised in-person control exam to confirm their places for 2026-2027, the university announced — and the fallout reached the top on Friday: Secretary General Patricia Dávila resigned, with Javier de la Fuente named as her replacement. Verification over expulsion: every selected student gets the chance to prove their spot in person.

🚨🇲🇽 <u>"EL R1" ALSO ORDERED THE FEMICIDE OF VALERIA MÁRQUEZ: HARFUCH</u>

The case against "El R1" keeps growing. The alleged CJNG cell leader captured this week for ordering the murder of Uruapan mayor Carlos Manzo also ordered the May 2025 femicide of influencer Valeria Márquez, Security Secretary Omar García Harfuch revealed — at the request of his own son, her former partner, who "ya la había amenazado de muerte en varias ocasiones." Two of Mexico's highest-profile killings, one alleged mastermind, and a state that is actually closing cases.

🔥🇲🇽 <u>SIX NAVY MEMBERS TESTIFY IN FARÍAS LAGUNA FUEL-GRAFT CASE</u>

The fiscal-huachicol investigation keeps pulling threads inside the Navy. Six Semar members gave ministerial statements for more than 11 hours before the FEMDO in the case against the Farías Laguna brothers — the network that siphoned 10 million liters from the tanker Challenge Procyon through shell companies and clandestine yards in Tampico-Altamira and Ensenada. Testimony that "opens new lines of analysis," according to the defense. Zero impunity does not exempt uniformed ranks.
banner: FUEL GRAFT: SIX NAVY OFFICERS TESTIFY

🇲🇽🇻🇪 <u>MEXICO SENDS TWO MORE NAVY SHIPS WITH AID TO VENEZUELA</u>

While Washington tightens its siege, Mexico's Navy keeps sailing south. Two more vessels departed for Venezuela on Friday, President Sheinbaum confirmed — days after the Isla Holbox and Huasteco returned home on July 24 from their own aid mission. Asked why Mexico also sent firefighters to Canada, she put the doctrine in one line: Mexico helps the nations of the world out of solidarity, "not because they are strategic partners."

🇲🇽📈 <u>PESO RALLIES TO 17.33 AFTER MEXICO'S GDP BEAT</u>

The Mexican peso gained 0.71% on Thursday to close at 17.3395 per dollar — a 12-centavo jump — after INEGI reported the economy grew 2.1% annually in the second quarter, well above the 1.6% the market expected and faster than the US economy's own 1.5%.

🇲🇽🚧 <u>BRUGADA TAKES THE WORKS PLAN TO MILPA ALTA'S PUEBLOS</u>

Clara Brugada brought the Casa por Casa program to San Bartolomé Xicomulco and left a full package: 45 km of road repaving starting in October, a special assembly to fix the drinking water supply, extended hours at the local clinic, 10 new RTP buses and a citizen consultation on bringing the Cablebús to the borough. "There is an obligation of the city government to attend to the original pueblos," she said. The program has already visited 380,000 homes across the capital.

🇲🇽🎓 <u>UNAM ORDERS IN-PERSON EXAM AFTER AI CHEATING SCANDAL</u>

UNAM will make selected applicants retake the admission exam in person after its technical commission found statistically atypical results in the 2026 online test. Applicants scoring 100 or more correct answers jumped from about 5% in 2021-2025 to 16.3% this year; those with 110+ went from 0.9% to 5.5% — a sixfold spike. Rector Leonardo Lomelí: "The seriousness of the situation demanded a fast but well-founded response that safeguards a fundamental principle: equity in access to higher education."

🇲🇽🛢️ <u>PEMEX POSTS 18 BILLION PESOS IN NET PROFIT, CUTS DEBT 9.1%</u>

Pemex just delivered its best semester in years: net profit of 18 billion pesos and operating profit of 85.5 billion in the first half of 2026, with revenues up 30.3% to 510.4 billion. Crude processing at Mexican refineries averaged over 1 million barrels a day, diesel output jumped 19.3%, and financial debt fell 9.1% from the end of 2025 — reversing the 11.1 billion operating loss it posted a year ago. The "bankrupt" company the right kept mourning is paying its own way.

🇲🇽🌎 <u>PERU'S NEW GOVERNMENT COMES KNOCKING: IT WANTS TIES WITH MEXICO BACK</u>

Peru's new foreign minister, Carlos Espá, says Lima is working to restore diplomatic relations with Mexico and Colombia. Ties collapsed in 2022, when Mexico stood by Pedro Castillo after the congressional coup and gave asylum to his family and former PM Betssy Chávez. Sheinbaum never bent and never recognized the coup governments. Four years later, it is Lima that picks up the phone.
